articles.title: Brain scans map multiple “low road” fear pathways between the human thalamus and amygdala
articles.summary: Animal studies have described “low road” pathways that rush sensory information from the thalamus to the amygdala. A brain imaging study of 113 people now maps several such routes in humans, with some far more consistent than others.

articles.title: New study suggests touch is a key ingredient in dogs’ stress-buffering power
articles.summary: Petting a dog after a stressful task didn’t speed recovery, but in a new experiment it was followed by calmer brain and heart responses when dog owners faced a second stress test soon after.

articles.title: Web Agent Agentic Reinforcement Learning Decision Model Under Multi-Cost and Failure Risk
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.23857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intelligent agent interactions in real-world web environments are commonly constrained by request budgets, time delays, anti-crawling restrictions, and operational failure risks. Strategies solely optimizing task success rates often exhibit unusable phenomena such as "high success but high cost" or "low risk but conservative failure." articles.title: PolyGraph: Plan-Buffered CUDA Graphs for Adaptive Speculative Decoding
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.23861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive speculative decoding changes the active batch size B and draft length d from one decode step to the next, whereas a CUDA Graph replays a fixed launch configuration. The resulting verification width M = B d forces serving systems to pre-capture many shapes, capture new ones on the serving path, or pad every step to the largest draft. We present PolyGraph, a plan-buffer mechanism for custom Triton kernels that avoids this choice. PolyGraph captures one maximum-grid graph and writes the active shape to GPU memory before each replay. Kernels

articles.title: Brain wave study reveals shifting auditory responses in children with ADHD
articles.summary: Children with ADHD process unexpected sounds differently than their peers, but these brain responses change as they grow. New research shows heightened sensitivity to sudden noises in early childhood gives way to blunted responses in middle childhood.

articles.title: College students who use more cannabis are less willing to share it, and less likely to use it with friends
articles.summary: Cannabis is often a group activity in college, but the pattern looks different among heavier users. Students who used more often shared less in a hypothetical sharing task and were less likely to use mostly with others.

articles.title: Online meat-shaming may do little to change minds, new research suggests
articles.summary: Telling someone online that they eat meat because they don’t care about the planet tends to backfire into defensiveness rather than persuasion. The same moral criticism from a stranger provoked even more pushback when it arrived as a private direct message instead of a public comment.

articles.title: How chronic drinking masks the brain’s hidden scars from childhood trauma
articles.summary: Childhood trauma leaves a physical mark on the brain's structure, but heavy drinking might hide the evidence. A new brain imaging study reveals how alcohol use disorder can overwrite the subtle neurodevelopmental scars left by early life abuse and neglect.

articles.title: Frontiers: A Roundtable Discussion on the I-Frame vs. S-Frame Debate
articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? articles.title: Your aging brain may be trading memory for something more valuable
articles.summary: The aging brain may be undergoing a remarkable transformation rather than simply losing its abilities, shifting its focus from remembering details to understanding the bigger picture. Scientists suggest this change could be an evolutionary adaptation that helps older adults develop wisdom and share decades of knowledge with younger generations.

articles.title: Scientists find a way to fight Alzheimer’s brain damage without removing toxic tau
articles.summary: Scientists have found a promising way to protect the brain from Alzheimer’s-related damage by blocking immune cells that contribute to the destruction of neurons. In mice, the treatment preserved roughly 40% more tissue in memory centers and improved memory, even without removing harmful tau protein buildup.

articles.title: They took a robot baby home for the weekend. By Monday, their testosterone responded differently
articles.summary: Childless couples who cared for a lifelike baby doll showed no testosterone change at first, but after a weekend with the doll at home, men’s and women’s levels fell by about 9 to 12 percent during joint caregiving.

articles.title: A bigger paycheck tends to come with personality changes, according to a large-scale analysis of psychology research
articles.summary: A meta-analysis of 11 long-running studies covering up to 134,515 workers found that rising pay tended to precede small gains in conscientiousness and emotional stability, along with slight drops in agreeableness and extraversion.
